33704.subject: Economics
33704.question_text: A shift in the demand curve indicates
33704.explanation:
A shift in the demand curve means that other determinants of demand other than price causes demand to change. They include changes in tastes, population, income, prices of substitute or complementary goods, and expectations about future conditions and prices. This is usually an indication of a change in demand.

A change in demand describes a shift in consumer desire to purchase a particular good or service, irrespective of the price difference.

34850.explanation: Joint demand is When two or more goods are jointly demanded to satisfy single need. Example demand for cars and petrol, pens and ink, tea and sugar, etc, computers and software. If the demand for car decreases, it will also affect the demand for petrol.

34851.subject: Economics
34851.question_text: Any price below the equilibrium price will lead to
34851.explanation: Any price below the equilibrium price will lead to excess demand with decrease in supply. This is so because, people generally buy more of a commodity when the price is low while suppliers will want to supply more when the price is high. Hence, for a price set below equilibrium, suppliers will cut back on producing more of that commodity while demand will be high.

34852.explanation: In a free market economy, the price mechanism regulates production and labor. Companies sell goods and services at the highest price consumers are willing to pay while workers earn the highest wages companies are willing to pay for their services.

34855.subject: Economics
34855.question_text: The law of diminishing marginal utility applies to a
34855.explanation: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that the marginal utility of a good or service declines as its consumption increases. This means that, as a consumer keeps consuming additional units of a commodity, the additional satisfaction derived will keep decreasing (goods become less valuable as you continue consuming more of it)

34856.subject: Economics
34856.question_text: why is the law of diminishing returns a short run phenomenon?
34856.explanation:
The law of diminishing returns states that as an increasing amount of a variable factor is added to a fixed factor, the marginal product of the variable factor may at first rise but must eventually fall.

The law of diminishing returns applies in the short run because only then is some factor fixed.
